title: Project Mining
lead: Turning a project directory of files into verbatim, searchable drawers.
summary: Project mining scans a directory tree, detects file formats via extension and content, chunks text into drawers, applies virtual line numbering for locators, and stores them idempotently in the palace. The process is incremental: re-mining the same project never duplicates drawers; it upserts to the same storage rows keyed by deterministic SHA-256 IDs. Gitignore rules, size limits, and chunk-cap safeguards prevent runaway ingest. Adjacent format extraction and mega-file splitting are siblings to the core miner, sharing chunking, entity detection, and room-routing logic.

concepts.definition: A single chunk of verbatim text from a source file, stored with metadata (wing, room, line range, date, entities). The atomic unit of search in the palace.

A searchable index of pointers linking a source file to its drawers. Each pointer includes extracted topics/entities, Tier 6a date:line locators, and drawer IDs. Drawers are materialized on search hit; closets are scanned first.
Line numbers added at read time (not stored on disk) when a drawer is retrieved. Enables Tier 6a closet pointers to jump to specific line ranges within a drawer without rewriting the stored text.

Re-mining the same file produces deterministic drawer IDs, so upsert to the same rows. The project miner uses source_file + chunk_index + SHA-256 to make IDs stable across re-runs. Mtime-based detection re-mines only if the file changed.
Content-aware routing that assigns each file to a room based on folder path (highest priority), filename, or keyword scoring in the first ~2000 chars. Falls back to 'general' if no match.
Automatic date extraction from filename, YAML frontmatter, content body, or mtime—in that priority order. Used to populate content_date in drawer metadata for Tier 6a closet pointers.

Tagging drawers with known-entity names (from ~/.mempalace/known_entities.json) plus capitalized words appearing 2+ times in the first 5000 chars of content. Filtered through COCA common-words list to drop noise.
Content-type categorization (emotional, technical, family, etc.) based on keyword scoring across the first 3000 chars. Rooms organize by TOPIC; halls organize by FEELING/TYPE.

symbols.name: process_file
symbols.role: Main entry point for ingesting a single file. Reads, chunks, detects room, builds metadata, upserts drawers and closets. Returns (drawer_count, room_name, skip_reason).

symbols.name: chunk_text
symbols.role: Splits content into drawer-sized chunks with configurable size/overlap. Prefers paragraph/line boundaries. Computes line_start/line_end via str.count for Tier 6a locators.

symbols.name: detect_room
symbols.role: Routes a file to a room via four-tier priority: folder path > filename > keyword scoring > fallback 'general'.

symbols.name: file_already_mined
symbols.role: Idempotency check. Returns False (re-mine) when: no drawers exist, normalize_version is stale, or mtime differs. Enables safe re-runs without duplicates.

symbols.name: build_closet_lines
symbols.role: Generates compact pointer lines from file content. Extracts topics, entities, quotes. Emits legacy 3-segment or Tier 6a 4-segment format based on metadata availability.

symbols.name: _extract_content_date
symbols.role: Five-tier date extraction: filename -> frontmatter -> content body -> mtime -> None. Returns ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' or None.

symbols.name: _extract_entities_for_metadata
symbols.role: Extracts entity tags from known-entity registry and capitalized words appearing 2+ times in first 5000 chars. Returns semicolon-separated string for metadata.

symbols.name: detect_hall
symbols.role: Routes content to a hall (emotional, technical, family, general) via keyword scoring in first 3000 chars.

symbols.name: GitignoreMatcher
symbols.role: Parses and matches .gitignore patterns. Handles negation, anchoring, directory-only rules, and ** wildcards.

symbols.name: mine_formats
symbols.role: Third miner for binary office documents. Walks directory, extracts text via MarkItDown/striprtf, chunks, routes to rooms, upserts drawers with extract_mode='format' scoping.

symbols.name: extract_text
symbols.role: Converts one file (PDF/DOCX/RTF/etc.) to text. Returns (text, ExtractionStatus). Handles 13 fringe cases (encryption, cloud files, missing deps, etc).

surprises.title: Drawer IDs are file+chunk, not timestamp-based
surprises.detail: Deterministic IDs (SHA of source_file + chunk_index) mean re-runs idempotently upsert without needing version fields or UUID tracking. A file moved to a different path produces a different drawer ID (intentional—it's a different source). The trade-off: if a user renames or relocates a source, old drawers remain orphaned until explicitly purged. This is acceptable because drawers carry source_file metadata for retrieval.

surprises.title: Mtime tolerance of <0.001s prevents spurious re-mines
surprises.detail: Without this tolerance, slow filesystems or CI environments could trigger redundant re-mines on every run even if the file wasn't actually modified. The tolerance accounts for filesystem timestamp precision (ext4 is nanosecond, NTFS is 100ns). This is a defense-in-depth measure against unnecessary embedding re-compute.

surprises.title: Chunk boundary logic prefers paragraph breaks over line breaks
Format miner is fully separate, not edits to miner.py
surprises.detail: Binary file extraction (PDF, DOCX, RTF) could have been bundled into miner.py, but instead lives in format_miner.py—a third parallel miner. This follows the existing miner-per-content-type pattern. The trade-off is code duplication, but the benefit is smaller review surface and failure isolation—a format-miner bug cannot affect project/convo mining.

surprises.title: RTF files bypass MarkItDown and use striprtf instead
surprises.detail: MarkItDown 0.1.5 cannot convert RTF (returns raw \rtf1\ansi control codes unchanged). format_miner routes .rtf to striprtf (line 387-390, verified empirically 2026-05-19 on 52 real RTF files). This per-format dispatch is invisible to callers—both transformers produce Markdown text that flows into the normal chunker.

designDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md explicitly states 'Incremental only — Append-only ingest after initial build. Never destroy existing data to rebuild. A crash mid-operation must leave the existing palace untouched.' Deterministic drawer IDs and mtime-based dirty detection enable safe re-runs. A crash mid-chunk-batch leaves completed batches intact; re-run resumes from the next uncompleted file.

designDecisions.decision: Virtual line numbering at read time, not stored on disk
designDecisions.rationale: Storing [N] prefixes in the drawer would couple presentation to storage, invalidate existing closet pointers on re-mine, and lose idempotence. Read-time numbering (via render_with_line_numbers) keeps the drawer verbatim, allows Tier 6a date:Lstart-Lend pointers to work, and is backward-compatible—callers that ignore line numbers see the same string back, just with [N] prefixes added.

designDecisions.decision: Closet pointers as compressed, searchable approximations
designDecisions.rationale: Closets are scanned (via FTS5) before drawers are opened. Each pointer extracts topics (action verbs, headers), entities (proper nouns), and quotes from the first ~5000 chars. The Tier 6a extension (date:Lstart-Lend) allows retrieval to jump to a specific line range. Pointers are intentionally approximate—'±2 off-by-one at boundaries is fine.' Exact positional indexing is deferred to Tier 7.

designDecisions.decision: Room detection via path/filename/content, in that priority order
designDecisions.rationale: Rooms are time-based groupings (day, session, topic). The priority (folder > filename > content) reflects user intent: a file in docs/frontend/ is intentionally routed to a 'frontend' room even if the content doesn't mention it. Content-keyword scoring is the fallback, not the primary signal, preventing false positives from occasional mentions.

designDecisions.decision: Format miner as a separate module, not integrated into miner.py
designDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md values 'Incremental only' and 'Verbatim always,' and the existing codebase follows a miner-per-content-type pattern. format_miner.py is a third instance of the same shape (scan -> transform -> chunk -> store). Separate modules allow smaller review surface, cleaner test isolation, and no risk of regressions in the stable project/convo miners.

related.why: Parallel miner for chat exports; shares chunking, entity extraction, room routing, and idempotent drawer logic with project miner
Project scanner detects projects/people via git history and manifests; extracted entities populate known_entities.json for metadata tagging during ingest
Closet pointers (topic|entities|date:Lstart-Lend|->ids) form the index layer that LLMs scan to locate relevant drawers without reading full content
Drawers are stored in wings/rooms; closets create searchable cross-references; halls link entities within a wing; tunnels link wings by topic or entity
Closets are scanned via FTS5; matching pointers trigger drawer retrieval; virtual line numbering applies when rendering results
Project mining is the main ingest path; incremental append-only design is a core architectural principle enforced across all miners

searchDoc.title: Project Mining
searchDoc.summary: Project mining scans a directory tree, detects file formats, chunks text into drawers with virtual line numbering, and stores them idempotently using deterministic SHA-256 drawer IDs. Re-mining never duplicates; it upserts to the same rows.
searchDoc.body: Project mining turns a directory of source files into verbatim, searchable drawers stored in the palace. The pipeline starts with scan_project, which walks the filesystem recursively, respects .gitignore rules, skips cache directories like .git, __pycache__, .venv and node_modules, ignores symlinks, filters by readable extension, and drops files larger than 500 MB. For each surviving file, process_file reads its bytes as utf-8 with errors replaced, then routes the file to a room via detect_room using a four-tier priority: folder path, filename, keyword scoring in the first 2000 characters, and a general fallback. Content is split by chunk_text into 800-character chunks with 128-character overlap, breaking at paragraph or line boundaries when possible. Each chunk gets 1-indexed line ranges computed with str.count to avoid quadratic slicing on huge files. Before writing, file_already_mined checks whether drawers already exist, whether the normalize version is stale, and whether the file mtime differs from the stored source_mtime within a 0.001-second tolerance. When a re-mine is needed it purges stale drawers and upserts fresh ones in batches of 1000. Drawer IDs are deterministic SHA-256 hashes of source_file plus chunk_index, so re-runs and parallel mines converge on the same rows without duplicates. Metadata enrichment via _build_drawer_metadata extracts a content_date through a five-tier hierarchy of filename, YAML frontmatter, content body, and mtime; tags entities from known_entities.json plus repeated capitalized words filtered by a COCA stoplist; and detects a hall by keyword scoring. After chunks are upserted, build_closet_lines produces compact pointer lines of the form topic|entities|date:Lstart-Lend|drawer_ids, with the Tier 6a date and line segment included only when metadata is present, and legacy three-segment pointers otherwise. Post-mine graph construction links wings sharing topics, builds within-wing entity hallways, and materializes cross-wing tunnels, all fault-tolerantly. The design is incremental and append-only: drawers are stored verbatim, line numbering is applied at read time, and a crash mid-batch leaves completed batches intact. Binary office formats are handled by a separate format_miner module using MarkItDown, with RTF routed to striprtf because MarkItDown cannot convert it.
